blocks.content: Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 lays down the duties, powers and functions of the Authority.

items: IRDAI was constituted following the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee report (1994).
Section 14 explicitly details the statutory powers and functions of IRDAI.
Minimum capital requirement for Life and General Insurers is ₹100 Crore, while for Reinsurers it is ₹200 Crore.
IRDAI headquarters were relocated from New Delhi to Hyderabad in 2001.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI is a statutory body established under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 to protect policyholders and regulate the insurance sector.
Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 grants powers to issue, renew, modify, suspend, or cancel registrations of insurance companies.
IRDAI sets qualifications, training standards, and codes of conduct for insurance agents, surveyors, and loss assessors.
The authority mandates the investment of funds by insurance companies and regulates the maintenance of margin of solvency.
IRDAI protects policyholders' interests regarding claim settlements, surrender values, and terms of policy contracts.
